cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Class modesty – The main theme of class modesty as explored and highlighted in 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' brilliantly dissects class modesty to build character depth as Ada Harris confronts overcoming class modesty with optimism to purchase a haute couture dress.

cosy-blockquote.p: haute couture – The main theme of haute couture as explored and highlighted in 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' brilliantly dissects haute couture to build character depth as Ada Harris confronts overcoming class modesty with optimism to purchase a haute couture dress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Optimism ≠ Pessimism – hopefulness and confidence about the future ≠ a tendency to see the worst aspect of things.

p.em: Example: Her natural optimism kept her going, whereas his pessimism made him want to give up.

cosy-blockquote.p: Trauma ≠ Healing – a deeply distressing or disturbing experience ≠ the process of making or becoming sound or healthy again.

p.em: Example: The protagonist struggles to overcome childhood trauma and begin a journey of emotional healing.

cosy-blockquote.p: Redemption – The main theme of redemption as explored and highlighted in 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' brilliantly dissects redemption to build character depth as Ada Harris confronts overcoming class modesty with optimism to purchase a haute couture dress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Guv'nor – (noun) British informal term of address for a boss or respected man.

p.em: Example: Mrs. Harris politely addresses her London employers with traditional working-class warmth.

cosy-blockquote.p: posh – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'posh' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-blockquote.p: charwoman – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'charwoman' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cinematic Medium – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'Cinematic Medium' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tonal Shift – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'Tonal Shift' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does the opening of 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' show the idea of class modesty? Practice with adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ If you were in 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris', how would you handle the challenges of class modesty?

How does the director introduce haute couture early in the movie? Focus on adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Have you ever faced a problem where you had to deal with haute couture?

As the story goes on, does optimism create problems for Ada Harris? Frame your answer with adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Does the way the movie shows optimism feel like real life to you?

How do the scenes in 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' show trauma between the main characters? Use adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ How do you personally keep trauma in balance in your life?

How does Ada Harris react to the challenge of redemption? Discuss using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ If you could change one decision made by Ada Harris about redemption, what would it be?

What clues and secrets about 'guv'nor' can you find in the movie? Use adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Have you ever used a word or expression like 'guv'nor' in your own life?

How does the script use the expression 'posh' to make the scene more interesting? Respond with adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Do you think learning casual words like 'posh' is helpful for fluency?

How does using 'charwoman' show the characters' real feelings during overcoming class modesty with optimism to purchase a haute couture dress? Formulate with adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Is there an equivalent word in your language for 'charwoman'?

How does learning the truth about 'cinematic medium' change what you think of the characters? Analyze with adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ When you want to express a feeling, do you use slang or direct words like 'cinematic medium'?

If they knew the truth about 'tonal shift' earlier, how would the story change? Speculate using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ What is your favorite line of dialogue from the movie 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris'?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
'Ada Harris's story of class modesty in 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' is very sad, and they should be more careful.' Do you agree? Use adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ If you were a director, how would you show the concept of class modesty?

'Ada Harris's movie makes the world look too beautiful, but it has a high cost.' Discuss using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Do you think the visuals of a movie are more powerful than the dialogue?

'Ada Harris is not a nice person because they only care about optimism.' Give your opinion using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Have you ever felt that a movie's alternative ending would be better?

'Ada Harris's movie 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' is too simple and does not show deep feelings about trauma.' Talk about this with adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ If you could choose a song from your life to match the theme of trauma, what would it be?

'Ada Harris's problem of overcoming class modesty with optimism to purchase a haute couture dress never ends because they cannot agree on redemption.' Explain using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ What was the most memorable scene in 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' that made you think?

'The film would be better if the director chose a different setting for 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris'.' Speculate using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Would you ever want to write a story based on your own life experiences?

'The secondary characters, like the elegant Dior staff, Marquis de Chassagne, and London friends, are more interesting than the main hero.' Evaluate with adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Which part of filmmaking (music, camera angles, lighting) has the biggest effect on you?

'The music and sound design are what make 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' a great movie.' Discuss using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ If you could change the cast of 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris', which actors would you choose?

'The recurring visual symbols are important to understand the film's deeper meaning.' Discuss using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ Do you enjoy analyzing movies or do you prefer to just watch the story?

'The story of 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris' is a critique of real-world human behavior.' Discuss using adjectives of Material, Origin & Order.
★ If you could save only one scene from 'Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris', which one would it be?

ul.li: Incorrect: They don't allow her leave the house → Correct: They don't allow her to leave the house (Use 'allow someone to do something' construction.)
Incorrect: He is making her to believe lies → Correct: He is making her believe lies (Use the bare infinitive after 'make someone do something'.)
Incorrect: I have seen that movie yesterday → Correct: I saw that movie yesterday (Use the simple past for actions completed in the past.)
